bills.title: Measures for the Collection Administration and Enforcement of Tax Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Tuan Liew Chin Tong (Timbalan Menteri Kewangan)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Income Tax Act 1967 (“Act 53”), the Real Property Gains Tax Act 1976 (“Act 169”), the Stamp Act 1949 (“Act 378”), the Labuan Business Activity Tax Act 1990 (“Act 445”), the Petroleum (Income Tax) Act 1967 (“Act 543”), the Customs Act 1967 (“Act 235”) and the Excise Act 1976 (“Act 176”). AMENDMENTS TO THE INCOME TAX ACT 1967 Part II of this Bill seeks to amend the Income Tax Act 1967. 2. Clause 4 seeks to introduce a new subsection (7) into section 77b of Act 53 to allow the Director General to remit the whole or any part of the increased sums under section 77b of Act 53. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 3. Clause 5 seeks to amend paragraph 82c(6)(b) of Act 53 to require an electronic commerce platform provider whether in Malaysia or outside Malaysia in respect of any goods sold or services performed by any other person to issue a self-billed invoice in accordance with the conditions as may be imposed by Director General. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 4. Clause 6 seeks to introduce a new subsection (2a) into section 107b of Act 53 to require an application under subsection 107b(2) for a variation of instalment payments to be furnished by an electronic medium or by way of electronic transmission in accordance with section 152a of Act 53. This amendment has effect for the year of assessment 2028 and subsequent years of assessment. 5. Clause 7 seeks to introduce a new subsection (4) into section 119b of Act 53 to empower the Director General to impose a penalty, if no prosecution is instituted, for non-compliance with rules made under paragraph 154(1)(c) of Act 53 relating to the automatic exchange of information and the furnishing of a country-by-country report. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 6. Clause 8 seeks to amend subsection 138(5) of Act 53 in the definition of “classified person” to expand the interpretation of officials and employee of the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia to include officials and employee who is no longer in service with the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 7. Clause 9 seeks to amend section 145 of Act 53. Subclause 9(a) seeks to amend subsection 145(1) of Act 53 to widen the scope of service of notices under Act 53 to include service by an electronic medium or electronic transmission. Subclause 9(b) seeks to introduce a new subsection (2a) into section 145 of Act 53 to provide that a notice relating to tax which is sent by an electronic medium or by way of electronic transmission shall be deemed to have been duly served on the person when a report confirming the delivery of the notice is generated by the designated information processing system as determined by the Director General. These amendments come into operation on 1 January 2027. 8. Clause 10 seeks to introduce a new subsection (1a) into section 202 of Act 53 to provide for the due date for a Constituent Entity to furnish its Top-up Tax return where the Constituent Entity is a member of two or more Multinational Enterprise Groups in a Financial Year— (a) in the case of Multinational Enterprise Groups having the same Financial Year, not later than fifteen months from the last day of the Financial Year; and Measures for the Collection, Administration and Enforcement of Tax (b) in the case of Multinational Enterprise Groups having different Financial Year, not later than fifteen months after the last day of the later Financial Year. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. AMENDMENTS TO THE REAL PROPERTY GAINS TAX ACT 1976 Part III of this Bill seeks to amend the Real Property Gains Tax Act 1976. 9. Clause 14 seeks to introduce a new subsection (7) into section 13a of Act 169 to allow the Director General to remit the whole or any part of the increased sums under subsection 13a(4) of Act 169. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 10. Clause 15 seeks to introduce a new subsection (1a) into section 24 of Act 169 to provide that where a disposer has furnished a return for a disposal and there is an excess payment of tax, such return shall be deemed to be a notification under subsection 24(1) and the disposer shall be deemed to have been notified of such excess on the day the return is furnished. This amendment has effect for the year of assessment 2027 and subsequent years of assessment. 11. Clause 16 seeks to amend subsection 27(1) of Act 169 to empower the Director General to also require any person to give orally any information in relation to a return made under Act 169. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 12. Clause 18 seeks to amend subsection 47(5) of Act 169 in the definition of “classified person” to expand the interpretation of official and employee of the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia to include official and employee who is no longer in service with the Inland Revenue Board of Malaysia. This amendment comes into operation on 1 January 2027. 13. Clause 19 seeks to amend section 53 of Act 169. Subclause 19(a) seeks to amend subsection 53(1) of Act 169 to widen the scope of service of notices under Act 169 to include service by an electronic medium or electronic transmission. Subclause 19(b) seeks to introduce a new subsection (2a) into section 53 of Act 169 to provide that a notice relating to tax which is sent by an electronic medium or by way of electronic transmission shall be deemed to have been duly served on the person when a report confirming the delivery of the notice is generated by the designated information processing system as determined by the Director General. These amendments come into operation on 1 January 2027. AMENDMENTS TO THE STAMP ACT 1949 Part IV of this Bill seeks to amend the Stamp Act 1949. 14. Clause 21 seeks to amend subsection 4a(2) of Act 378 to be in line with current stamping practice where adhesive stamp is no longer in use. This amendment comes into operation on 1 J

bills.title: Finance Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Tuan Liew Chin Tong (Timbalan Menteri Kewangan)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Income Tax Act 1967 (“Act 53”), the Stamp Act 1949 (“Act 378”), the Labuan Business Activity Tax Act 1990 (“Act 445”), the Petroleum (Income Tax) Act 1967 (“Act 543”) and the Finance Act 2025 (“Act 874”). AMENDMENTS TO THE INCOME TAX ACT 1967 Chapter II of this Bill seeks to amend the Income Tax Act 1967. 2. Clause 4 seeks to amend paragraph 6(1)(i) of Act 53. Subclause 4(a) seeks to clarify the tax treatment of income distributed by a unit trust under section 61A of Act 53 to non-resident unit holders. Such income will be subject to tax at the rates prescribed in Part X of Schedule 1, with the tax collected through the withholding tax mechanism provided in section 109D. Subclause 4(b) seeks to specify that the revised tax rates for certain categories of non-resident unit holders will take effect for the year of assessment 2027 and subsequent years of assessment, while the existing tax rates applicable to non-resident companies continue to apply from the year of assessment 2016 onwards. These amendments have effect for the year of assessment 2027 and subsequent years of assessment. 3. Clause 5 seeks to introduce new paragraphs (t), (u) and (v) into subsection 39(1) of Act 53. Paragraph 39(1)(t) seeks to disallow a deduction for any outgoings and expenses incurred by a company, whether directly or by way of reimbursement, in respect of any right granted to any employee of the company by reason of any office or employment held in Malaysia by the employee to acquire new shares issued by the company. Paragraph 39(1)(u) seeks to disallow a deduction for any payment made by a company to its holding company or subsidiary company in respect of newly issued shares of the holding company or subsidiary company that are issued to the employee of the company making such payment, subject to any rules prescribed by the Minister. These amendments have effect for the year of assessment 2027 and subsequent years of assessment. Paragraph 39(1)(v) seeks to disallow a deduction for any payment specified in paragraph 13(1)(a) of Act 53 paid to an employee in the form of money other than the payment made through an account opened by a financial institution in the name of the employee. This subclause shall not apply to any amount paid by a micro enterprise and small and medium enterprise. This amendment has effect for the year of assessment 2028 and subsequent years of assessment. 4. Clause 6 seeks to amend section 46 of Act 53. Subclause 6(a)(i) seeks to amend paragraph 46(1)(a) of Act 53 to increase the amount of personal relief available to an individual for a year of assessment from nine thousand ringgit to twelve thousand ringgit. Subclause 6(a)(ii) seeks to amend paragraph 46(1)(c) of Act 53 to provide that the claim for carer expenses for the care of parents and grandparents does not require the certification of a medical practitioner that the conditions of the parents or grandparents require a carer. Subclause 6(a)(iii) seeks to substitute paragraph 46(1)(f) of Act 53 to expand the scope of relief allowed in respect of education undertaken by an individual, his spouse and his child. Subparagraph 46(1)(f)(i) of Act 53 seeks to provide for the claim for relief under this subparagraph can be made for any course of study in any field undertaken at the level of certificate, diploma, bachelors, masters or doctorate degree at any institution or professional body in Malaysia recognised by the Government or approved by the Minister. Subparagraph 46(1)(f)(ii) of Act 53 seeks to provide that the claim for relief under this subparagraph can be made for any course of study for the purpose of upskilling or self-enhancement in the field of technical or vocational recognised under the National Skills Development Act 2006 which is limited to a maximum amount of three thousand ringgit. Subparagraph 46(1)(f)(iii) of Act 53 seeks to provide that the claim for relief under this subparagraph can be made, limited to a maximum amount of two thousand ringgit— (a) for any course, training, skill or self-enhancement class not related to employment undertaken by an individual and his spouse; and (b) for any course, training, class or tuition in the fields of science, technology, engineering, mathematics, arts, languages or religion undertaken by the individual’s child. Finance53 Subclause 6(a)(iv) seeks to amend paragraph 46(1)(g) of Act 53 to expand the scope of individual relief for health expenses expended by an individual and his spouse. Subparagraph 46(1)(g)(v) is introduced into paragraph 46(1)(g) of Act 53 to provide for a relief for expenses for the purchase either by the individual for his wife or by the wife for herself of breastfeeding equipment used for the individual’s child aged two years and below which is limited to a maximum amount of one thousand ringgit. Subparagraph 46(1)(g)(vi) is introduced into paragraph 46(1)(g) of Act 53 to provide for a relief for expenses for the post-natal care services provided by a care centre or any individual registered, recognised or licensed under any written law relating to such services which is limited to a maximum amount of three thousand ringgit. Subclause 6(a)(v) seeks to substitute paragraph 46(1)(n) of Act 53 to expand the scope of existing personal deduction to include contributions made or suffered by an individual to the Social Security Organization in relation to the industries specified in paragraphs 1, 9 and 10 of the First Schedule to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017. This subclause also seeks to provide for an additional personal deduction of one hundred and fifty ringgit to an individual in respect of contributions for injury occurring outside the course of employment under the Employees’ Social Security Act 1969, or contributions in relation to the industries specified in the First Schedule to the Self-Employment Social Security Act 2017, other than the industries specified in paragraphs 1, 9 and 10, made or borne by that

bills.title: Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons (Amendment) Act 2026
bills.presenter: Datuk Seri Dr. Shamsul Anuar bin Haji Nasarah (Timbalan Menteri Dalam Negeri)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Registration of Criminals and Undesirable Persons Act 1969 (“Act 7”) to provide for registrable particulars of a person convicted of registrable offence becoming spent. 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and the provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 7 to introduce the definition of “crime-free period” for the purposes of the new provisions relating to registrable particulars becoming spent. 4. Clause 3 seeks to introduce new sections 13a, 13b and 13c into Act 7. The proposed new section 13a seeks to provide for registrable particulars becoming spent, including the eligibility requirement, applicable crime-free period and circumstances under which the registrable particulars cease to be eligible to become spent. The proposed new section 13b seeks to provide for the effect of registrable particulars of a person convicted of a registrable offence becoming spent. Upon the registrable particulars becoming spent, the registrable particulars shall be treated as no longer registered in the register and as if the person has not been convicted of the registrable offence to which the spent registrable particulars relate. The new section 13b further provides even though the registrable particulars has become spent, the registrable particulars shall remain recorded in the register for the purposes of record by the Registrar. The proposed new section 13c seeks to provide that the registrable particulars of a person which has become spent shall be revived if during or after the expiry of a crime-free period, the person is convicted of any registrable offence specified in the First Schedule. The proposed new section also seeks to provide that if the registrable particulars of the person is revived, the registrable particulars of the person shall be treated as if they have never become spent under Act 7. 5. Clause 4 seeks to amend subsection 15(1) of Act 7 to empower the Minister to amend the proposed new Fourth Schedule. 6. Clause 5 seeks to introduce a new Fourth Schedule into Act 7 to provide the list of registrable offences for which registrable particulars are not eligible to become spent. 7. Clause 6 deals with saving provision.

bills.title: Sport Development (Amendment) Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Dr. Mohammed Taufiq Johari (Menteri Belia dan Sukan)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Sports Development Act 1997 (“Act 576”), among others, to introduce a new part relating to enforcement and investigation, to provide for the management and disposal of asset, and liabilities of a sports body the registration of which has been revoked to protect the creditor’s interest and stakeholder, and to provide for the institution of prosecution. This proposed amendment also to empower the Minister to make regulations in respect of compliance with international obligations in relation to anti-doping and any matter relating to safe sport. 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and provision on the commencement of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 576 by inserting the new definition of “Court” means the High Court. 4. Clause 3 seeks to substitute subsection 3(2) of Act 576 to provide that the Minister may issue guidelines consistent with international guidelines or rules. 5. Clauses 4, 5 and 6 seek to amend subsections 8(2), 9a(2) and 9b(2) of Act 576 to substitute the term “athletics competitions” with “sporting events” to ensure uniformity and accuracy in the usage of terminology and to avoid confusion with the sport of athletics specified in the First Schedule to the Act 576. 6. Clause 7 seeks to introduce new sections 19a, 19b and 19c into Act 576. The proposed new section 19a seeks to provide for matters relating to the movable and immovable property of a sports body, legal capacity of a sports body to sue and be sued, judgment and execution of judgment against a sports body, criminal liability of a member of a sports body and the dissolution of a sports body. The proposed new section 19b seeks to empower the Commissioner to issue a written direction to a sports body requiring the sports body to amend its constitution or rules within the time specified in the direction after taking into consideration the representation made by the sports body. The proposed new section 19c seeks to provide that a sports body shall not change its name, place of business, registered address or correspondence address or amend its constitution or rules without prior approval of the Commissioner. This clause also provides for the non-compliance with this new proposed section as an offence. 7. Clause 8 seeks to introduce new sections 25a, 25b and 25c into Act 576. The proposed new section 25a seeks to provide for the consequences of the revocation of registration of a sports body by the Commissioner or by virtue of the order made by the Minister under section 41a, including the vesting of property in the Director General of Insolvency for the purpose of winding up the affairs of the sports body. This clause also empowers the Commissioner and Director General of Insolvency to require any information relating to the property, affairs, business, accounts or books of the sports body, or any other matters relating to the sports body. This clause also provides for the non-compliance with subsection 25a(2) as an offence. The proposed new section 25b seeks to provide for the procedure for the vesting of the assets, debts and liabilities of a sports body the registration of which has been revoked in a new registered sports body, subject to an application by the new sports body to the Director General of Insolvency who will then apply for an order from the High Court. The proposed new section 25c seeks to provide for the inspection of any document filed with the Commissioner and enable any person to obtain any copy of the document upon receipt of the prescribed fee subject to the conditions specified in subsection 25c(2). 8. Clause 9 seeks to introduce a new Part VIa into Act 576 which consists of new sections 32a, 32b, 32c, 32d, 32e, 32f, 32g and 32h. The proposed new section 32a seeks to provide for the appointment of enforcement officers by the Minister. The proposed new section 32b seeks to empower an enforcement officer or police officer to carry out any investigation and enforcement of any provision under Act 576. The proposed new section 32c seeks to provide that an enforcement officer shall declare his office and produce his authority card when exercising his powers under Act 576. The proposed new section 32d seeks to provide for the power of enforcement officer or police officer to examine any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of a case and to record any statement made. This clause also provides that any statement made by the person examined shall be admissible as evidence under Act 576 in any proceedings in court. The proposed new section 32e seeks to provide for the power of enforcement officer or police officer to require any person to submit to him any book, minute book, register, financial statement, document, any particular or other things whether in physical or electronic form, and the enforcement officer or police officer may inspect, make copies of, take extracts from, remove and detain any book, minute book, register, financial statement, document, particular or other things whether in physical or electronic form. The proposed new section 32f seeks to provide for the seizure of any book, minute book, register, etc., if the enforcement officer or police officer has reason to believe that an offence has been committed under Act 576. This clause also provides that any book, minute book, register, etc., seized shall be admissible as evidence in any proceedings in court. bills.presenter: Datuk Seri Dr. Haji Dzulkefly Ahmad (Menteri Kesihatan)
bills.explanation: This Bill seeks to amend the Food Act 1983 (“Act 281”). 2. Clause 1 contains the short title and commencement of the proposed Act and empowers the Minister to appoint different dates for the coming into operation of different provisions of the proposed Act. 3. Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2 of Act 281 by introducing the definition of “food contact material” and amending the definitions of “advertisement”, “import”, “label”, “seal”, “sell or sale” and “importer” consequential to the insertion of the definition of “food contact material”. This clause also seeks to amend the definitions of “authorized officer” and “premises” and delete the definition of “Director” in line with the Ministry of Health’s current policy. 4. Clause 3 seeks to amend section 3 of Act 281 to enable the Minister to authorize any public officer to procure samples of food contact materials in relation to any matter which appears to the Minister could affect the general interests of consumers of food contact materials. 5. Clause 4 seeks to amend section 4 of Act 281 to expand the powers of authorized officers to include the investigation of food and food contact materials. This clause also seeks to address advertising issues and grants power to authorized officers to order the appearance of any person acquainted with the facts and circumstances of a case. Clause 7 seeks to amend section 7 of Act 281 to provide that any method of analysis which is prescribed by regulations shall be expanded to include food contact materials. 8. Clause 8 seeks to amend section 8 of Act 281 to strengthen control of food and food contact materials comprehensively by expanding the power of authorized officers to call for information from persons who are in possession of food and food contact materials for advertising purposes. 9. Clause 13 seeks to introduce a new section 11a into Act 281 to provide for the closure of premises that prepare or sell food containing substance injurious to health. 11. Clause 23 seeks to amend section 17 of Act 281 to clarify the offence provision in respect of advertisement. This clause also seeks to introduce new subsection (1a) into section 17 for the offence that relates to advertisement in respect of food contact materials. 17. Clause 30 seeks to introduce a new section 29a into Act 281 to provide for rules regulating the importation of food contact materials into Malaysia which includes labelling and relabelling as well as offences relating to it. 23. bills.title: National Trust Fund Bill 2026
bills.presenter: Tuan Liew Chin Tong, Timbalan Menteri Kewangan
bills.explanation: The National Trust Fund Bill 2026 (“the proposed Act”) seeks to repeal the National Trust Fund Act 1988 [Act 339] (“the repealed Act”) and reestablish the National Trust Fund (“the Fund”). Under the proposed Act, the Fund will continue to be maintained and replenished since the utilisation of RM5 billion from the Fund for the purchase of Covid-19 vaccines in 2021. The proposed Act also seeks to incorporate the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) as the governing body of the Fund and provide for the investment of the Fund. The proposed Act aims to ensure the continued growth of the Fund. Strict conditions and procedures are imposed for the utilisation of the Fund as the Fund is intended to serve as a long-lasting financial reserve for the benefit of current and future generations of Malaysia. The proposed Act also seeks to introduce reform of the Fund in three main aspects: (a) placing contributions to the Fund on a broad and mandatory statutory footing, beyond voluntary payments; (b) preserving the Fund’s capital by limiting annual withdrawal to one-half of its expected real return and confining its use to only education, healthcare and climate change mitigation and adaptation purposes; and National Trust Fund 25 (c) establishing the Board of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) (“the Board”) with clear duties and powers and strengthening its functions regarding investments of the Fund. Part I 2. Part I of the proposed Act deals with preliminary matters. 3. Clause 1 contains the short title of the proposed Act and seeks to empower the Minister to appoint a date for the commencement of the proposed Act. 4. Clause 2 contains the definitions of certain words and expressions used in the proposed Act. Part II 5. Part II of the proposed Act deals with the National Trust Fund and its governance and contains twenty-one provisions divided into two Divisions. Division 1 6. Division 1 of Part II deals with the provisions relating to the National Trust Fund. 7. Clause 3 seeks to provide for the reestablishment of the Fund. Moneys standing in or due to be paid to the National Trust Fund under the repealed Act shall be transferred to the Fund. As at 31 December 2024, the National Trust Fund’s net assets at the group level amounted to RM22.43 billion. 8. Clause 4 seeks to provide for the contributions to the Fund. Subclause 4(1) places the contributions on a broad and mandatory statutory footing, in place of the voluntary basis under the repealed Act. Since the establishment of the National Trust Fund in 1988, Petroliam Nasional Berhad (PETRONAS) has been its sole contributor, with the contribution amount varying from year to year at the discretion of the Board of PETRONAS. This clause requires contributions by the Federal Government of, firstly a minimum of 0.1% of its projected annual revenue, secondly a minimum of 2% of the dividend received from PETRONAS, and thirdly a minimum of 2% from the export duty received by the Federal Government on depleting resources. Under clause 2, “depleting resources” is defined as crude oil, mineral ores, iron ore or any other natural resources which may be susceptible to depletion. For clarification, the contribution amount linked to export duty is computed only on the portion forming part of the revenue of the Federal Government and does not affect any portion of the duty assigned to a State Government under Article 110 of the Federal Constitution. 9. Clause 5 seeks to provide for other contributions which may be voluntarily paid into the Fund, namely contributions by any State Government which derives royalty from petroleum or other depleting resources and income from investments of the Fund. This clause was provided for in the repealed Act and is adopted into the proposed Act. 10. Clause 6 seeks to provide for expenditure to be charged on the Fund. 11. Clause 7 seeks to empower the Minister to require the Board to furnish returns, reports, accounts and other information in respect of the Fund. Division 2 12. Division 2 of Part II deals with the provisions relating to the National Trust Fund (Incorporated). 13. Clause 8 seeks to provide for the incorporation of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) as a body corporate having perpetual succession and a common seal, with power to hold property and to sue and be sued in its own name. This confers legal personality to the National Trust Fund (Incorporated). 14. Clause 9 seeks to provide for the functions and powers of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated), that is to administer, manage and invest the Fund. 15. Clause 10 seeks to provide for the common seal of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) and for its authentication. 16. Clause 11 seeks to provide for the appointment of the Board of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) (“the Board”), which shall consist of a Chairperson, a Deputy Chairperson who is an officer of the Ministry of Finance, an officer from the Prime Minister’s Department, and between two to four persons with the knowledge, experience and expertise in business, investment, banking or finance. All members are to be appointed by the Minister. 17. Clause 12 seeks to provide for the duties and powers of the Board. The Board shall primarily be responsible for the administration and management of the National Trust Fund (Incorporated) and investment of the Fund. Subclauses 12(2) and 12(3) seek to allow the Board to delegate any of its powers to any person as it deems necessary, subject to the approval of the Minister. However, such delegation does not preclude the Board from exercising the powers so delegated. Subclause 12(5) seeks to empower the Board to establish committees to assist in the performance of its duties and the exercise of its powers. 18. Clause 13 seeks to provide for the remuneration of members of the Board. National Trust Fund 27 19. Clause 14 seeks to provide that a member of the Board shall hold office for a term not exceeding three years and be eligible for reappointment, but no
